text: Databases store and organise information so we can find it quickly. In a SQL database, data lives in tables with rows and columns, like a spreadsheet. You use queries to ask questions, such as finding all customers from one city. NoSQL databases are more flexible and often store data as documents instead of tables. Before building a database, you plan its structure through data modelling. Finally, indexes help the database find data faster, but they also take extra space. Choosing the right type depends on your needs.
